title: Standard cotangent resolution chain projection by face differences
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings. Use the standard augmented simplicial polynomial $A$-algebra $Q_n=(F_AU)^{n+1}B$ and its alternating differential complex $K^{-n}=M_n=\Omega^1_{Q_n/A}\otimes_{Q_n}B$ from [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], with $F_A(E)=A[E]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Put $R=Q_0=A[B]$, let $\epsilon:R\twoheadrightarrow B$ be evaluation, and set $I=\ker\epsilon$. Write $Q_1=A[R]$ with variables $Y_p$, $p\in R$, and $Q_2=A[Q_1]$ with variables $Z_f$, $f\in Q_1$; $X_b$ denotes a variable of $R$. The faces satisfy $d_0(Y_p)=p$, $d_1(Y_p)=X_{\epsilon(p)}$, and the three faces of $Z_f$ are $f,Y_{d_0f},Y_{d_1f}$. Let $\partial_1:M_1\to M_0$ and $\partial_2:M_2\to M_1$ be the alternating face differentials, and let $\delta:I/I^2\to M_0$ send $[h]$ to $\mathrm dh\otimes1$. The rule $\rho(\mathrm df\otimes b)=b[d_0(f)-d_1(f)]$ is a well-defined $B$-linear map $M_1\to I/I^2$ satisfying $\delta\rho=\partial_1$ and $\rho\partial_2=0$. Thus $c^{-1}=\rho$, $c^0=1_{M_0}$, and zero lower components define a chain map $c:K\to[I/I^2\xrightarrow{\delta}M_0]$ in degrees $-1,0$. These chain maps commute strictly with the standard semilinear resolution maps for every commutative ring square $A\to A'$, $B\to B'$, with the target viewed as a $B$-complex by restriction of scalars.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] for the augmented simplicial algebra and its alternating differential. Evaluation is surjective since $\epsilon(X_b)=b$. Writing $e_1=\epsilon d_0=\epsilon d_1:Q_1\to B$, the evaluation faces give $d_0(Y_p)=p$, $d_1(Y_p)=X_{\epsilon(p)}$ and $d_0(Z_f)=f$, $d_1(Z_f)=Y_{d_0f}$, $d_2(Z_f)=Y_{d_1f}$. These formulas on variables determine the faces by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. In particular both faces $Q_1\to R$ agree after augmentation.

source.place: Tag 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map), explicit downward arrow; expanded verification.

proof.text: The quotient $I/I^2$ is a $B$-module: define $b[h]=[rh]$ for any lift $\epsilon(r)=b$; changing $r$ changes $rh$ by an element of $I^2$. By the Leibniz rule of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $\mathrm d(uv)\otimes1=\mathrm du\otimes\epsilon(v)+\mathrm dv\otimes\epsilon(u)=0$ for $u,v\in I$. Since $I^2$ consists of finite sums of such products, $h\mapsto\mathrm dh\otimes1$ kills $I^2$. Also $\mathrm d(rh)\otimes1=\epsilon(r)(\mathrm dh\otimes1)$ for $h\in I$. This proves that the stated $\delta:I/I^2\to M_0$ is well-defined and $B$-linear.

source.place: Tag 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map), explicit downward arrow; expanded verification.

proof.text: Put $\Delta(f)=[d_0f-d_1f]\in I/I^2$. Give this module its $Q_1$-action through $e_1$. Additivity of the faces gives additivity of $\Delta$; their agreement on $A$ gives $\Delta(a)=0$. Expanding the product gives $d_0(fg)-d_1(fg)=d_0(f)(d_0g-d_1g)+d_1(g)(d_0f-d_1f)$. Reducing modulo $I^2$, multiplication by either $d_0f$ or $d_1f$ on $I/I^2$ is multiplication by $e_1(f)$; hence $\Delta(fg)=e_1(f)\Delta(g)+e_1(g)\Delta(f)$. Thus $\Delta$ satisfies exactly the derivation relations of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials].

source.place: Tag 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map), explicit downward arrow; expanded verification.

proof.text: Apply the universal property in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] to $\Delta$ to obtain a $Q_1$-linear map $u:\Omega^1_{Q_1/A}\to I/I^2$, $u(\mathrm df)=\Delta(f)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-universal-property] to $Q_1\xrightarrow{e_1}B$ and $u$. In the tensor order used here this is the same universal property with $\omega\otimes b$ in place of $b\otimes\omega$; its inverse is given by swapping the two factors, which respects the balancing relation. It yields the unique $B$-linear map $\rho:M_1\to I/I^2$ with $\rho(\mathrm df\otimes b)=b\Delta(f)$. In particular its formula respects both the differential relations and tensor balancing.

source.place: Tag 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map), explicit downward arrow; expanded verification.

proof.text: On every generator $\mathrm df\otimes b$ the definition of $\delta$ gives $\delta\rho(\mathrm df\otimes b)=\mathrm d(d_0f-d_1f)\otimes b$. The alternating differential from [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] gives the same result for $\partial_1$. The presentation of differentials in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and tensor bilinearity show that these elements generate $M_1$ over $B$ (a scalar coefficient of a differential moves to the tensor factor through $e_1$). Therefore $\delta\rho=\partial_1$.

source.place: Tag 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map), explicit downward arrow; expanded verification.

proof.text: The elements $\mathrm dZ_f\otimes b$ generate $M_2$: every polynomial is a finite sum of monomials by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and repeated additivity and the Leibniz rule of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] express its differential in the variable differentials. Now $\partial_2(\mathrm dZ_f\otimes b)=\mathrm df\otimes b-\mathrm dY_{d_0f}\otimes b+\mathrm dY_{d_1f}\otimes b$. Applying $\rho$ gives $b$ times the class of $(d_0f-d_1f)-(d_0f-X_{\epsilon(d_0f)})+(d_1f-X_{\epsilon(d_1f)})=0$, since $\epsilon(d_0f)=\epsilon(d_1f)$. Thus $\rho\partial_2=0$. Together with the preceding equality these are precisely the two potentially nonzero chain-map conditions; all other conditions have both sides zero.

source.place: Tag 08UP (remark-explicit-comparison-map), explicit downward arrow; expanded verification.

proof.text: For a ring square write $\alpha:A\to A\prime$, $\beta:B\to B\prime$. The standard semilinear maps $t_n:Q_n\to Q_n\prime$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence] commute with faces and augmentations. Thus $t_0(I)\subset I\prime$ and $t_0(I^2)\subset(I\prime)^2$, giving $\bar t_0:I/I^2\to I\prime/(I\prime)^2$, $[h]\mapsto[t_0h]$, which is $\beta$-semilinear. The differential map is $T_n(\mathrm df\otimes b)=\mathrm d(t_nf)\otimes\beta(b)$; its well-definedness follows directly from the differential relations in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and tensor balancing. On generators, $\bar t_0\rho(\mathrm df\otimes b)=\beta(b)[t_0d_0f-t_0d_1f]=\beta(b)[d_0\prime t_1f-d_1\prime t_1f]=\rho\prime T_1(\mathrm df\otimes b)$, and $T_0\delta([h])=\mathrm d(t_0h)\otimes1=\delta\prime\bar t_0([h])$. These are equalities of maps, not merely homotopies. The degree-zero components of $c$ are identities and the lower components are zero, so the entire square of chain maps commutes strictly after restriction of target scalars.
